title: Diamond Framework: Reputation-Weighted Validator Selection via Verifiable Non-Transferable Reputation
description:
Proof-of-stake secures admission and deterrence with a single instrument, financial capital, and that is the source of its structural tension: high collateral requirements deter honest but capital-constrained validators, low requirements expose the network to Sybil attacks. The Diamond Framework replaces a fraction of the financial stake with verifiable, non-transferable reputation, so the admission barrier falls without claiming that the full Cost of Attack is preserved; that question is left open in the paper.

This deposit is the frozen PDF snapshot of the manuscript, v0.2.3, with its source. v0.2.3 is an errata release and changes no contract and no test. The paper had printed 286,144 gas as the deployed verification cost; that figure belongs to V3's three-input verifying key, while the key the registry installs has four public inputs and measures 306,253 gas cold and 247,211 warm. The installed key's figure is now the deployed one (break-even 730 gwei, 29x margin at 25 gwei, the ingest at 2.2x the verification), and 286,144 is kept only where the text says it is V3's: measured on 2026-10-20 at commit 70f225c, with a three-input key the registry can no longer install. The full admission path is measured for the first time: manager.admit costs 395,255 gas cold for a first admission under the installed key (break-even 566 gwei). No conclusion of the paper moves: verification stays more than two orders of magnitude below the ingest and Bulletproofs stays roughly an order of magnitude above it.

Artifact: diamond-framework-2026-10-29.pdf, 43 pages, 601340 bytes, SHA-256 dd071071bf3b300d50b1355d3c094a84dcdd8ad708dfbf3d7b58a6a748d313d9; source main.tex, 158063 bytes, SHA-256 21efaaf021407fe7ac513d96e8e83c1fc5682e6c3d3105ea265d0a1d0f97812c. The claim registry that binds each quantitative claim to the script reproducing it is sealed by an eleven-file anchor root (SHA-256 6fe5884baeb214ebbee99a4ed14c6b0189bc8c6f2c73cadfafad7c772e13937b). An OpenTimestamps receipt over that root was stamped on 2026-10-30 (four pending attestations, zero Bitcoin confirmations at seal time); the receipt over the preceding root (76e95f6d...) attests that root and is not cited as evidence for these bytes. The v0.2.2 record is not rewritten either; a metadata notice in that record points here.

Verification is offline and reproducible: 316 Foundry tests (0 failed, 1 skipped), the numerical suite (38 scripts in the manifest, byte-identical reruns) and an 11/11 audit gate. Limits are declared rather than omitted: the Groth16 verifier deployed on the Avalanche Fuji testnet uses a committed development key, carries no ceremony and has recorded no certified admission; the recursive option and Teleporter cross-subnet latency remain deferred; and the external audit is pending. Bitcoin enters only as an external witness of the anchor, because a receipt sealed inside the root it witnesses would be circular.
